chapter: Father, Bay St. Louis and family language
title: Father's career: traveling shows and Promo's band
summary: Tio says his father did not conduct, traveled widely with a minstrel show, played the Minnie Ha Ha solo, had Tio and Dublade band years earlier and led a Bay St. Louis band.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Did your father play in this symphony orchestra too? Or did he ever conduct any?

No. No. My father, he, he did not conduct any, that I know of. Probably when he was, he was, he traveled a great deal. He traveled partly all over the United States. He traveled with great shows such as Billy Cassandra.
Oh yes, I've heard people talk about that show.
Yeah. He traveled with, he traveled with, he's a fellow who played, my father was a man who played a solo of Minnie Ha Ha. That's a very, very complicated piece of music.

Minnie Ha Ha. And I don't know what he meant to have that copy yet. And that was an arrangement that was all written by my father and my uncle. They didn't have, they just had a suit. They had, they just had a suit and copy of it. And that was written by them. They were married to Northern Ireland.
It seems to me more of the old time musicians, they all talk about your brother as, usually they refer to him as the most famous one of the clarinetists in the family.
That's right. He was. Not saying in prison or trying to any book here, that family, he was one of the greatest.

You don't have to because everybody else does. He could tell that if he was down here and getting the street behind him when they had five or six others supposed to be great out there. That's what he used to tell who was who.

That's right. I was wondering more about your father now. Quite a few people will tell us about your uncle Papa, they call him, didn't they? That's right. That he played in some of the dance bands and other bands that they talk about. But very few people tell us which bands your father worked with. Did he ever do much dance work? Or a brass band?

That's right. My father, my father from the time, they were one of the greatest bands of all of them. That was the time of Teo and Dublade. They had a band of the arms. That's been a long time. Then my father. Then my father, he was a, he was a, had a band, Promo's band.
Promo's band. That was Bay St. Louis.
Then he traveled so much that he went with, he was with a show and a, Billy Cassand show.
and Richard and Pringle. That's probably why we don't hear so much about him.
He was traveling all over around St. Francisco and Mexico. He was all over, part of all over the United States.
